Selected lecture decks from ECON3111. Shared for study and reference. Please cite
appropriately and do not redistribute commercially.

```{=html}
<ul class="rec-list">
<li class="rec">
  <div class="rec-year">Lecture 1</div>
  <div class="rec-body">
    <p class="rec-title">Foundations and rational choice under certainty</p>
    <p class="rec-finding">The neoclassical benchmark and why it matters; descriptive against normative theories; preferences as relations; completeness and transitivity; and where behavioural evidence comes from. Includes worked activities and a validity map of methods.</p>
    <p class="rec-links"><a href="/assets/teaching/econ3111-week1-foundations.pdf">Slides (PDF)</a></p>
  </div>
</li>
<li class="rec">
  <div class="rec-year">Lecture 6</div>
  <div class="rec-body">
    <p class="rec-title">Advanced choice under risk and uncertainty</p>
    <p class="rec-finding">Expected utility as a benchmark and the independence axiom; the Allais and Ellsberg paradoxes; probability weighting; prospect theory, covering reference dependence, loss aversion and weighted probabilities; and ambiguity with multiple priors. Includes worked numerical examples and exam practice.</p>
    <p class="rec-links"><a href="/assets/teaching/econ3111-week6-risk-uncertainty.pdf">Slides (PDF)</a></p>
  </div>
</li>
</ul>
```

## Related reading

The [writing](/blog/) covers several of these ideas in plain language, including
the [certainty effect](/blog/posts/why-99-does-not-feel-like-100/), the
[Allais paradox](/blog/posts/the-allais-paradox/), the
[Ellsberg paradox](/blog/posts/the-ellsberg-paradox/),
[loss aversion](/blog/posts/loss-aversion-in-health-and-policy/) and
[risk against ambiguity](/blog/posts/risk-versus-ambiguity/).
